transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess I'm here because... I just can't seem to keep myself together lately. My daughter left for basic training recently, and ever since then, I feel like I just come home to a dead house. 

It's really messing with my day-to-day. I've been sitting out in my truck crying before my shifts start. I'm missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years, and I'm snapping at the younger guys on the crew for no real reason. And outside of work, I’ve just stopped doing anything. I haven't gone out on the water or worked on my metal sculptures... I just don’t see the point right now. I figured I needed to talk to somebody before I completely fall apart.
How long have you been feeling this way since your daughter left for basic training?
It’s been about a month. She left four weeks ago, and... yeah, I’ve been struggling like this pretty much since the day she shipped out.
Are you still able to enjoy the things you normally like to do, or has that changed for you lately?

Like I mentioned a minute ago, it's definitely changed. I haven't been doing any of the stuff I usually like. I haven't taken the boat out, haven't touched my metal sculptures... I just don't have the desire to do any of it right now. I don't really get any enjoyment out of anything since she left.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

No, not really. Like I said, I just... I don't look forward to anything right now. There's nothing I'm doing that makes me feel good or gives me any kind of pleasure. I just go to work, come home, and that's it.
Have you had any thoughts about harming yourself since your daughter left?
No, I haven't. I mean, I feel terrible and I'm struggling, but I haven't had any thoughts about hurting myself or anything like that. I just... I miss her, and it's hard, but I wouldn't do that.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since your daughter left?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I'm still eating my normal meals, I guess. And my sleep... I mean, I sleep fine. I still get my regular hours every night and wake up for work okay. So, no, those haven't really changed.
Do you feel like you're a burden to others?

No, I don't think so. I mostly just keep to myself right now anyway. Like I said, I just go to work and come back to an empty house. I'm not really asking anyone for help or putting my stuff on other people, so... no, I wouldn't say I feel like a burden.
Do you feel guilty about anything lately?
No, not really. I mean, I don't feel guilty. I just feel sad that she's gone. There's nothing I really did wrong, she just grew up and moved out. So... no, no guilt. Just missing her.
Do you feel like you're unable to function or make decisions most days?

Yeah, I guess I am struggling with that. At work, my supervisor actually took me off a complex welding job recently. He told me I wasn't coordinating safely enough... which is a big deal in my line of work. And even outside of work, I had a metal sculpture submission coming up, but I just... I let the deadline pass without finishing it. I just couldn't get it done. So, yeah, functioning and actually finishing things has been really hard lately.
Do you feel like your sadness is constant throughout the day?

No, I wouldn't say it's constant. I mean, when I'm at the shop and actually busy with a job, I'm focused on the metal and the tools, so I'm not really thinking about it. It's more when I clock out and come back to that empty house. That's when it really hits me. So, no, it's not all day long.
Have you been feeling worthless?

No, I wouldn't say worthless. I mean, I know I'm a good worker—even if I'm having a hard time focusing lately—and I know I raised a good kid. So I don't feel like I have no worth. It's just... I just feel really lost right now, not worthless.
Have your feelings of sadness and emptiness lasted all day, every day, since your daughter left?

No, not all day, every day. Like I said before, when I'm working, I can usually tune it out. It's really just when I'm alone and have time to think about the fact that she's gone. That's when the sadness takes over. But no, it's not every single minute of the day.
Do you feel like your current state is the worst you've ever felt in your life?

I'm not really sure if I'd call it the absolute worst I've ever felt in my whole life. I mean, I've had some rough patches before. But... it's definitely bad. I haven't really sat down and compared it to other times, to be honest. I just know that right now, it's really tough to get through those evenings. So, I don't know if it's the worst ever, but it's heavy.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, that if you were to do them now, you think you might still enjoy, even if you're not feeling like doing them?

I'm really not sure. I haven't tried doing much of anything besides work since she moved out. I mean, I used to like just relaxing, maybe watching a movie or tinkering with things in the garage, but... I don't know if I'd actually enjoy it right now even if I forced myself to do it. I just haven't had the drive to try and find out.
Are there any small pleasures in life, like a favorite food or a beautiful sunset, that you still find enjoyable?

I haven't really noticed, to be honest. I eat because I have to, but I'm not really paying attention to how it tastes or looking forward to it. And I haven't been paying much attention to things like sunsets. I just go to work, come home, and try to get through the evening. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm finding much enjoyment in those little things right now.
Are there any activities or things that you used to find pleasurable, but now you don't?

I don't really have a good answer for that. Like I said, I haven't really tried doing much of anything since she left. I used to like watching movies or messing around in the garage, but since I haven't even tried to do them, I can't say for sure if I'd still like them or not. I just haven't had the energy to even attempt it.
Are there any activities that you think you would normally enjoy, but now you don't find pleasure in them?

I think that's kind of what I was just getting at. I don't really know, because... well, I just haven't been doing my normal stuff. I go to my job, and then I come home and just sit. I haven't tried doing the things I normally enjoy, so I can't say for sure if I'd get pleasure out of them right now or not. I just haven't had the energy to even test it out.
Are there any activities that you think might bring you some happiness if you were to do them, even if you don't feel like doing them right now?

I honestly don't know. I can't really picture anything making me happy right now. Even if I forced myself to go out or... or try to do something fun, I just feel like I'd be going through the motions. It's hard to imagine getting any real joy out of anything when everything just feels so heavy.
Are there any activities that you normally enjoy, but now you find you are unable to derive pleasure from them?

I feel like you're asking me the exact same thing again, and I... I really don't have a different answer for you. Like I've been saying, I honestly just don't know. I haven't tried doing any of my normal stuff to even find out if I'd enjoy it right now. I just go to work, come home, and sit. That's really all I've got in me.
